site_article.headline: OpenAI wins Anthropic customers with steep discounts, report says
site_article.dek: Rippling, DataCamp and Replit have shifted AI spending toward OpenAI after price cuts, according to The Information.
site_article.summary: OpenAI is using aggressive discounts to move large customers away from Anthropic, The Information reported on October 24, 2026. Rippling says OpenAI now handles 52% of its coding work, up from 16% in May, and DataCamp says its costs fell by 80% to 90%.
site_article.seo_title: OpenAI discounts pull Rippling, DataCamp, Replit from Anthropic
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI is winning Anthropic customers with discounts. Rippling moved most coding work to OpenAI and DataCamp says costs fell 80% to 90%.
site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI is offering deep discounts to large business customers, and several, including Rippling, DataCamp and Replit, have moved much of their AI spending away from Anthropic as a result, according to The Information.
site_article.hero_alt: Two hands holding interlocking white and black puzzle pieces, one with an orange symbol and one with the OpenAI logo.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI is pulling large business customers away from Anthropic by offering steep discounts on its AI models, The Information reported on October 24, 2026. The Decoder, summarizing that report on October 25, named Rippling, Replit and DataCamp among the companies that have shifted spending toward OpenAI.

The clearest example comes from Rippling. In May 2026, Anthropic models powered 57% of the coding work done by Rippling's engineers, while OpenAI models handled 16%. By late October, those shares had nearly reversed, with OpenAI at 52% and Anthropic at 18%, according to chief executive Parker Conrad.

Conrad attributed the change to cost, according to The Information as cited by FourWeekMBA. The report frames the result as evidence that OpenAI's effort to undercut Anthropic on price is producing results.
DataCamp said OpenAI's pricing reduced its costs by 80% to 90%, according to chief executive Jonathan Cornelissen as reported by The Decoder.

Replit moved most of its AI spending from Anthropic to OpenAI after OpenAI offered a discount of more than 30% on model prices under a contract worth more than $100 million a year, The Information reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Replit, OpenAI and Anthropic have not publicly confirmed those financial terms, RuntimeWire noted. Replit chief executive Amjad Masad has cited cost, performance and partnership as reasons for making OpenAI the preferred provider for Replit Agent.

The deals also reach beyond software companies. A US bank with more than $7 billion in assets had its ChatGPT seats doubled to 500 employees at no additional charge, according to the report. The bank pays less than $7 per user, compared with the usual price of $20 or more.

The Decoder described OpenAI as partly buying market share at the expense of its own margins, while also noting real price reductions in its Sol and Luna model lines that OpenAI attributes to more efficient models and infrastructure. The same report said Anthropic's growth slowed from the second quarter to the third, according to an investor memo, and that low-cost Chinese models from DeepSeek and Kimi are adding price pressure on both companies.

Customer concentration makes these shifts significant. Estimates from YipitData, cited by FourWeekMBA, suggest the top 1% of Anthropic customers account for nearly half of its spend, and a letter from Ramp said 1% of firms drive 80% of spending on OpenAI and Anthropic.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the report shows the enterprise AI market starting to behave like a classic cloud price war. When a small group of very large buyers drives most of the revenue, winning a handful of contracts can move market share quickly, and price becomes a strong lever. For customers, the immediate effect is lower bills and more bargaining power. For the two labs, it raises the question of how long deep discounts can be sustained while both are spending heavily on computing power.

The next signal to watch is whether Anthropic responds with its own discounts or price cuts, and whether more large customers publicly report moving coding and agent workloads between the two companies.
